accepted.question_text: In the Tower of Hanoi problem, a state distributes finitely many differently sized discs among pegs, and a legal move transfers one top disc to another peg without placing a larger disc on a smaller disc; a perfect state has all discs stacked on one peg in legal order. For the four-peg Tower of Hanoi subproblem of moving n discs from a perfect state onto two different pegs in the shortest possible way, is the standard split strategy always optimal: choose a suitable division of the perfect tower into two parts, first solve the perfect-to-perfect Tower of Hanoi problem for the smaller discs using four pegs, then leave those smaller discs fixed, and solve the ordinary three-peg problem for the larger discs?
accepted.context_brief: Four-peg Tower of Hanoi split hypothesis

evidence.quote: No disc must ever be placed on a smaller one.
dividing the perfect state in a suitable way into two parts
The validity of this hypothesis is the most interesting open problem about the TH.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Although the number of cases for the less straightforward irregular-state shortest-path problem can be limited, it is not clear whether there are shortest path problems with even three different solutions.
